subject: How best to get the output from Linux 'script' command cleaned up.

messages.author: 0a26429513db9cdf
messages.subject: How best to get the output from Linux 'script' command cleaned up.
parts:
Hi all,

I am transitioning to command line and want to save my sessions.  I found the 'script' command will do so but the resulting 'output' file has a ton of control characters.  If I view the 'output' file with '>cat output' from Bash prompt it is displayed properly, but if I view it in vim or put it up on github it has ton of control characters.  After googling I tried  'unix2dos' function (it is helpful only with cleaning line breaks), and 'col -bp < output' will clean only some of the garbage/control character.  Best so far is a perl function I found on stackoverflow (below)

#!/usr/bin perl
while (<>) {
s/ \e[ #%()*+\-.\/]. |
\r | # Remove extra carriage returns also
(?:\e\[|\x9b) [ -?]* [@-~] | # CSI ... Cmd
(?:\e\]|\x9d) .*? (?:\e\\|[\a\x9c]) | # OSC ... (ST|BEL)
(?:\e[P^_]|[\x90\x9e\x9f]) .*? (?:\e\\|\x9c) | # (DCS|PM|APC) ... ST
\e.|[\x80-\x9f] //xg;
1 while s/[^\b][\b]//g;  # remove all non-backspace followed by backspace
print;
}

This function deletes some good code as well though, (this is a good time to start learning enough perl regular expression to modify such functions to work for me), is there another command or trick someone knows of that can help me here.

For more details about the things I need to fix in the perl function above that I borrowed from stackoverflow, when run it on the 1st chunk below it returns the 2nd chunk, while 3rd chunk is what is ought look like:

Chunk1(output of script command in vim)
> tbl(my_db, "batting") %>% collect(n=Inf) %>% summarize_if(is.numeric, funs(mean))^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^H^[[1P^H^[[1P^[[1@n^[[1@f^M
# A tibble: 1 x 14^M
    yearID    stint        G       AB        R        H     `2B`     `3B`^M
     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>^M
1 1964.262 1.077838 51.34344 141.9055 18.81554 37.13993 6.289167 1.293252^M
# ... with 6 more variables: HR <dbl>, RBI <dbl>, SB <dbl>, CS <dbl>, BB <dbl>,^M
#   SO <dbl>^M
> tbl(my_db, "batting") %>% collect(n=Inf) %>% summarize_if(is.numeric, funs(mean))^H^H,))^H^Hm))^H^Ha))^H^Hx))^H^H^M

Chunk2(output with perl function run on it)
> tbl(my_db, "batting") %>% collect(n=Inf
# A tibble: 1 x 14
    yearID    stint        G       AB        R        H     `2B`     `3B`
     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>
1 1964.262 1.077838 51.34344 141.9055 18.81554 37.13993 6.289167 1.293252
# ... with 6 more variables: HR <dbl>, RBI <dbl>, SB <dbl>, CS <dbl>, BB <dbl>,
#   SO <dbl>
> tbl(my_db, "batting") %>% collect(n=Inf) %>% summarize_if(is.numeric, funs(mean,max

Chunk3(What the actual input-output was, I can get this by issuing '>cat output' from Bash prompt)
> tbl(my_db, "batting") %>% collect(n=Inf) %>% summarize_if(is.numeric, funs(mean))                                                                                                                                            
# A tibble: 1 x 14
    yearID    stint        G       AB        R        H     `2B`     `3B`
     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>
1 1964.262 1.077838 51.34344 141.9055 18.81554 37.13993 6.289167 1.293252
# ... with 6 more variables: HR <dbl>, RBI <dbl>, SB <dbl>, CS <dbl>, BB <dbl>,
#   SO <dbl>
> tbl(my_db, "batting") %>% collect(n=Inf) %>% summarize_if(is.numeric, funs(mean,max))


This is encouraging.  Learning perl regular expressions I can get the function to do what I need in this specific case but best option would be if there is a way to change the file format or some such trick that will help me upload my sessions to github (can I save the file with specific extension that allows me to view the file upload to github with rawgit).  What I am thinking with rawgit is that if can view the proper output in Linux with '>cat output' maybe it can be rendered into the correct format for rawgit to know how to render it correctly.  Thanks again.

Best,
Sher

Script seems to be a way to  record a whole session  ( both input and output) which I don't think is what you want to do.

print ("oh hey, didn't see you there")
EOF

R CMD BATCH testscript.R
cat testscript.Rout




On Thu, Sep 21, 2017 at 8:04 PM, Balsher Singh <bls...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
Hi all,

I am transitioning to command line and want to save my sessions.  I found the 'script' command will do so but the resulting 'output' file has a ton of control characters.  If I view the 'output' file with '>cat output' from Bash prompt it is displayed properly, but if I view it in vim or put it up on github it has ton of control characters.  After googling I tried  'unix2dos' function (it is helpful only with cleaning line breaks), and 'col -bp < output' will clean only some of the garbage/control character.  Best so far is a perl function I found on stackoverflow (below)

#!/usr/bin perl
while (<>) {
s/ \e[ #%()*+\-.\/]. |
\r | # Remove extra carriage returns also
(?:\e\[|\x9b) [ -?]* [@-~] | # CSI ... Cmd
(?:\e\]|\x9d) .*? (?:\e\\|[\a\x9c]) | # OSC ... (ST|BEL)
(?:\e[P^_]|[\x90\x9e\x9f]) .*? (?:\e\\|\x9c) | # (DCS|PM|APC) ... ST
\e.|[\x80-\x9f] //xg;
1 while s/[^\b][\b]//g;  # remove all non-backspace followed by backspace
print;
}

     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>^M

# ... with 6 more variables: HR <dbl>, RBI <dbl>, SB <dbl>, CS <dbl>, BB <dbl>,^M
#   SO <dbl>^M
> tbl(my_db, "batting") %>% collect(n=Inf) %>% summarize_if(is.numeric, funs(mean))^H^H,))^H^Hm))^H^Ha))^H^Hx))^H^H^M

Chunk2(output with perl function run on it)
> tbl(my_db, "batting") %>% collect(n=Inf
# A tibble: 1 x 14
    yearID    stint        G       AB        R        H     `2B`     `3B`
     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>

#   SO <dbl>
> tbl(my_db, "batting") %>% collect(n=Inf) %>% summarize_if(is.numeric, funs(mean,max

Chunk3(What the actual input-output was, I can get this by issuing '>cat output' from Bash prompt)
> tbl(my_db, "batting") %>% collect(n=Inf) %>% summarize_if(is.numeric, funs(mean))                                                                                                                                            
# A tibble: 1 x 14
    yearID    stint        G       AB        R        H     `2B`     `3B`
     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>

# ... with 6 more variables: HR <dbl>, RBI <dbl>, SB <dbl>, CS <dbl>, BB <dbl>,
#   SO <dbl>
> tbl(my_db, "batting") %>% collect(n=Inf) %>% summarize_if(is.numeric, funs(mean,max))


This is encouraging.  Learning perl regular expressions I can get the function to do what I need in this specific case but best option would be if there is a way to change the file format or some such trick that will help me upload my sessions to github (can I save the file with specific extension that allows me to view the file upload to github with rawgit).  What I am thinking with rawgit is that if can view the proper output in Linux with '>cat output' maybe it can be rendered into the correct format for rawgit to know how to render it correctly.  Thanks again.

Sher
